portName: Port of Lisbon (Lisbon Cruise Terminal, Jardim do Tabaco)
seoTitle: Lisbon cruise port guide: Alfama, tram 28 and Belém
seoDescription: Lisbon cruise port 2026: 14 min walk to Praça do Comércio, Alfama on the doorstep. Tram €3.30 on board, 24h Carris/Metro €7.25, Jerónimos €18.
quickAnswer: Most ships dock at the Lisbon Cruise Terminal at Jardim do Tabaco, at the foot of Alfama; Praça do Comércio is a flat 14-minute walk along the river. Buy a €0.50 Navegante Ocasional card and load a 24-hour Carris/Metro ticket for €7.25 (2026), which covers trams 28 and 15E and the metro. From Belém, start back at least 2 hours 15 minutes before all-aboard; from Sintra, 3 hours.
intro: Lisbon is a docking port with the old town on the quay. Alfama climbs straight up behind the terminal and the castle is a steep walk of about 15–20 minutes, so you can be on the walls before the coaches arrive. The choice is between staying central (Alfama, the castle, the Baixa and tram 28) and heading west to Belém for the Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower, which reopened in May 2026 with timed entry. Sintra works only on a long call. Note that all four of Lisbon's historic lifts and funiculars, including the Santa Justa lift and the Glória funicular, are out of service in 2026, and the Glória is not expected back before 2029.

terminals.name: Lisbon Cruise Terminal (Jardim do Tabaco)
terminals.notes: The main terminal, opened in 2017 on Avenida Infante Dom Henrique. Most calls use it. Exit, turn left and follow the river to Praça do Comércio (about 14 minutes). Alfama starts across the road. Santa Apolónia metro (Blue line) is about 7 minutes' walk. Carris buses stop outside, and taxis wait in front.

terminals.name: Santa Apolónia (TPSA)
terminals.notes: Passenger terminal opposite Santa Apolónia station, within walking distance of the main terminal. Used for smaller ships. Same routes into town as Jardim do Tabaco.

terminals.name: Alcântara (TPA)
terminals.notes: The older terminal west of the centre, used when the main berths are full. Too far to walk to Alfama comfortably. Tram 15E runs along the riverside road towards the Baixa and Belém, and Alcântara is also on the Cascais train line. Hop-on hop-off red line buses stop here.

terminals.name: Rocha Conde de Óbidos (TPR)
terminals.notes: Overflow quay for two ships, west of the centre near Santos. Served by Carris buses and the Cascais line train via Santos station. Check your daily programme for the terminal.

walkability.detail: From Jardim do Tabaco, the riverside walk to Praça do Comércio is flat and about 14 minutes. Alfama is directly behind the terminal: cut through to Largo do Chafariz de Dentro, then it is a steep climb of about 8 minutes to Miradouro de Santa Luzia and 6 more to the castle. Pavements are polished limestone cobbles, slippery when wet. From Alcântara or Rocha, use public transport.

transportSections.time: 14 min to Praça do Comércio; about 15–20 min uphill to the castle
transportSections.detail: The simplest option from Jardim do Tabaco and Santa Apolónia. Wear shoes with grip; the cobbles are steep and smooth in Alfama.

transportSections.cost: €0.50 for the card; single Carris/Metro ticket €1.90; 24h Carris/Metro €7.25; 24h Carris/Metro/CP €11.40 (2026)
transportSections.time: Buy at any metro station machine
transportSections.detail: A reusable paper card that holds one product at a time. The €1.90 single is valid for one hour after first validation on Carris buses, trams and the metro. The 24-hour ticket starts at first validation and pays off after three tram rides. The 24h Carris/Metro/CP version adds CP suburban trains such as the Sintra and Cascais lines. You can also load stored credit (zapping), which is cheaper per trip than paying on board. Touch the card on the reader every time you board.

transportSections.cost: €3.30 on board (2026), or included in the 24h ticket
transportSections.time: Slow in traffic; allow plenty of time for the full Martim Moniz–Prazeres route
transportSections.detail: The historic tram through Graça, Portas do Sol, the Sé, Baixa, Chiado and Estrela. The Martim Moniz terminus is about 22 minutes' walk from the terminal and has the longest queues. Board mid-route instead, for example at the Sé or Portas do Sol, and ride west. It is the city's worst spot for pickpockets.

transportSections.cost: €3.30 on board (2026), or included in the 24h ticket
transportSections.time: About 38 min from Praça do Comércio to Jerónimos
transportSections.detail: Modern trams from Praça da Figueira to Algés along the river, via Praça do Comércio and Belém. Get off at the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos stop. Busy when big ships are in, so go early.

transportSections.cost: €2.30 on board (2026), or included in the 24h ticket
transportSections.detail: Stops outside the cruise terminal and runs west along the river to Belém (Jerónimos) and LX Factory. A useful direct return from Belém when the 15E is packed.

transportSections.time: A few minutes between central stations
transportSections.detail: Santa Apolónia (Blue line) is about 7 minutes' walk from Jardim do Tabaco. The Blue line runs to Terreiro do Paço, Baixa-Chiado and Restauradores (for Rossio station and the Sintra train). Not all stations are step-free.

transportSections.cost: Zone fare on the Navegante card, or the 24h Carris/Metro/CP ticket at €11.40 (2026)
transportSections.detail: Frequent trains from Rossio station, next to Restauradores metro. In Sintra the palaces are on the hill above the town; allow for the climb or the local bus.
Licensed taxis wait in front of the terminal. Uber and Bolt work across Lisbon and are often the easiest way back from Belém if you are running late.

returnTiming.rule: For a 17:30 all-aboard: leave Belém by 15:15, leave Alfama or the Baixa by 16:00, and be on a Sintra train back to Rossio by 14:30.
returnTiming.detail: Tram 15E from Belém to Praça do Comércio is about 38 minutes, plus the 14-minute walk to the terminal and queues. From Sintra, the train is about 40 minutes, then metro from Restauradores to Santa Apolónia and a short walk; Sintra counts as a train-dependent trip, so plan to be on board 90 minutes before all-aboard.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a licensed taxi or call an Uber or Bolt. If you are stuck in Sintra, a taxi is the only quick option. Call the port agent number in your daily programme if you will be late.

excursionAdvice: Lisbon is one of the easiest ports in Europe to do alone: the terminal is in town, transport is cheap and the main sights are on two tram lines. A ship tour is worth it for Sintra on a short call, because the palaces sit on a hill above the station and timed tickets plus a train make the return tight. It also suits anyone who cannot manage steep cobbles, since the city's lifts and funiculars are out of action in 2026.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at Jardim do Tabaco at 08:00, on a day other than Monday (Jerónimos is closed on Mondays), with a timed Jerónimos ticket booked for about 12:15.

steps.what: Walk off the ship, cross into Alfama via Largo do Chafariz de Dentro and climb to Miradouro de Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol.
Castelo de São Jorge at opening, before the coaches. About an hour on the walls.
Walk down past the Sé (cathedral) into the Baixa, along Rua Augusta to Praça do Comércio.
Buy a Navegante Ocasional card with a 24h ticket if you have not already, and take tram 15E from Praça do Comércio to the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos stop (about 38 minutes).
Jerónimos Monastery cloister; the church next door is free.
Lunch and custard tarts in Belém, then walk the riverside to the Monument to the Discoveries and Belém Tower (timed entry; book ahead if you want to go inside).
Start back: bus 728 towards the cruise terminal, or tram 15E to Praça do Comércio and walk 14 minutes along the river.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Alfama and the miradouros
sights.why: Lisbon's oldest quarter, directly behind the cruise terminal, with viewpoints at Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol over the river.
sights.tip: Walk up early, then come down through the lanes. The Feira da Ladra flea market runs on Tuesdays and Saturdays at Campo de Santa Clara.

sights.name: Castelo de São Jorge
sights.why: The castle on the highest hill of the old town, with the widest view of the city.
sights.tip: Open 09:00–21:00 from March to October, to 18:00 in winter. Lisbon residents now pay too, so queues are longer than they used to be. Go at opening.

sights.name: Baixa and Praça do Comércio
sights.why: The grid of streets rebuilt after the 1755 earthquake, from the riverside square up Rua Augusta to Rossio.
sights.tip: Rua Augusta restaurants with no prices on the menu are the classic overcharge; eat a few streets back.

sights.name: Tram 28
sights.why: The yellow historic tram through Graça, Alfama, the Baixa, Chiado and Estrela.
sights.cost: €3.30 on board, or included in the €7.25 24h ticket (2026)
sights.tip: Skip the Martim Moniz queue; board mid-route and keep your bag in front of you.

sights.name: Jerónimos Monastery
sights.why: Manueline monastery in Belém with a richly carved cloister and a free-to-enter church.
sights.cost: €18 adult; €9 aged 13–24 and 65+; under 13 free; church free (2026)
sights.tip: Open 09:30–17:30, last entry 17:00. Closed on Mondays. Entry is by timed slot; book online in advance.

sights.name: Belém Tower
sights.why: The 16th-century fortress tower on the river at Belém, reopened on 27 May 2026 after works.
sights.cost: Charged; check the official booking site
sights.tip: Now limited to about 900 visitors a day in half-hour slots. Book ahead or just see it from outside.

sights.name: Lisbon Cathedral (Sé)
sights.why: The city's cathedral, on the tram 28 route between Alfama and the Baixa.
sights.cost: Charged for the cloister and treasury; check on the day
sights.tip: Easy stop on the walk down from the castle.

sights.name: Sintra (option on a long call)
sights.why: Hill town of palaces and gardens, including Pena Palace, about 40 minutes by train from Rossio.
sights.cost: Train fare plus palace tickets; book palaces on the Parques de Sintra site
sights.tip: Only worth it on a call of 9 hours or more. Be on a train back by 14:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard.

beaches.name: Carcavelos and Cascais
beaches.howToGetThere: CP Cascais line train from Cais do Sodré, covered by the 24h Carris/Metro/CP ticket.
beaches.cost: Free beach; train fare or the €11.40 24h ticket (2026)
beaches.note: Lisbon has no city beach. These Atlantic beaches west of the city are the nearest sand; only worth it if you skip the sights.

food.where: Pastéis de Belém, Rua de Belém, next to the Jerónimos Monastery
A Ginjinha, Largo de São Domingos, by Rossio

commonMistakes.mistake: Queuing for tram 28 at Martim Moniz.
commonMistakes.fix: Board mid-route at the Sé or Portas do Sol, or ride early in the morning.

commonMistakes.mistake: Paying €3.30 on board for every tram ride.
commonMistakes.fix: Buy a €0.50 Navegante Ocasional card and load the €7.25 24h Carris/Metro ticket at a metro machine (2026).

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning on the Santa Justa lift or the Glória and Bica funiculars.
commonMistakes.fix: All were closed after the September 2025 Glória accident and none had reopened as of September 2026; the Glória is not expected back before 2029. Walk, or use trams and the metro.

commonMistakes.mistake: Going to Belém on a Monday.
commonMistakes.fix: Jerónimos is closed on Mondays. Do Alfama and the castle instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at Jerónimos or Belém Tower without a timed ticket.
commonMistakes.fix: Book online in advance; Belém Tower is capped at about 900 visitors a day.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to fit Sintra into a short call.
commonMistakes.fix: Allow at least 5–6 hours and be on a train back by 14:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard, or take the ship's tour.

safety: Lisbon is generally safe for daytime visitors; the main problem is pickpocketing. Tram 28 is the highest-risk spot, followed by tram 15E, the Green line metro, Praça do Comércio, Rua Augusta, Cais do Sodré and the queues at Jerónimos and the castle. Keep bags zipped and in front, and phones out of back pockets. Martim Moniz, Intendente and Anjos can feel rough late at night, which is not an issue on a cruise day. The cobbles are slippery, especially after rain: falls are a more likely problem than crime.
scams: Men offering hashish or cocaine in the Baixa, around Rossio and Praça da Figueira and in Bairro Alto. What they sell is fake, often soap or worse. Say no and keep walking.
Tuk-tuk drivers quoting high prices for short rides once you are on board. Agree the price, in writing, before you get in.

Restaurants on Rua Augusta and other tourist streets with no prices on the menu, then a large bill. Check prices before ordering; bread, olives and cheese put on the table are charged if you eat them.
Clipboard 'petition' collectors near tourist sites who distract you while someone else goes through your bag. Do not stop to sign.
accessibility: The Jardim do Tabaco terminal is modern, with automated walkways; ask security at the entrance for wheelchair help. The riverside walk to Praça do Comércio is flat and the Baixa grid is fairly level. Alfama, the castle and Chiado are steep with uneven cobbles, and in 2026 the Santa Justa lift and the Glória, Bica and Lavra funiculars are all closed; the newer Graça funicular reopened on 30 April 2026. The metro is not fully step-free. Modern trams on line 15E are easier to board than the historic tram 28 cars. A taxi to the castle gate or a ship coach tour is the practical choice for limited mobility.
rainyDay: Lisbon's cobbles are slippery in rain, so keep walking to a minimum. Good indoor options: the Jerónimos Monastery (closed Mondays) and the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum, which reopened on 18 July 2026 after renovation (Observador / Time Out Lisboa, July 2026). Do not plan on the National Tile Museum: it has been closed for restoration since November 2025, with no reopening date announced as of August 2026. The National Museum of Ancient Art (MNAA) has been closed since 29 September 2025, with reopening expected in late 2026, and the National Archaeology Museum has been closed since April 2022 (Lusa, August 2026). The Time Out Market at Cais do Sodré works for a covered lunch. Tram 15E to Belém is a dry way to see the riverside.
crowdTips: Tram 28 is fullest from mid-morning to late afternoon, especially when several ships are in; ride before 09:30 or board mid-route. Jerónimos and Belém Tower use timed tickets, and Belém Tower is capped at about 900 visitors a day since reopening in May 2026, so book ahead. The castle is busiest late morning; go at opening. Praça do Comércio and Rua Augusta are crowded all day. Since April 2024 Lisbon has charged a tourist tax on disembarking cruise passengers over 13, collected through the port and usually built into your cruise fare or port charges.

faqs.q: Is Lisbon cruise port walkable to the city?
faqs.a: Yes, from Jardim do Tabaco and Santa Apolónia. Praça do Comércio is a flat 14-minute walk along the river, and Alfama starts across the road. From Alcântara or Rocha Conde de Óbidos, take tram 15E, a bus or a taxi.
No. Ships dock alongside at the Lisbon Cruise Terminal (Jardim do Tabaco), Santa Apolónia, Alcântara or Rocha Conde de Óbidos.

faqs.q: How do I get from Lisbon cruise port to Belém?
faqs.a: Walk to Praça do Comércio and take tram 15E to the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos stop (about 38 minutes), or take bus 728 from outside the terminal. Fares are €3.30 on the tram and €2.30 on the bus if paid on board, or use a €7.25 24h Carris/Metro ticket (2026).
€3.30 paid on board, or included in the €7.25 24h Carris/Metro ticket loaded on a €0.50 Navegante Ocasional card (2026).

faqs.q: Do cruise passengers pay Lisbon's tourist tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Since April 2024 Lisbon has charged a tourist tax (introduced at €2) per disembarking cruise passenger aged over 13. It is collected through the port and normally included in your cruise fare or port charges, so you do not pay it in town.

faqs.q: Can I visit Sintra from a cruise ship in Lisbon?
faqs.a: On a long call, yes. The train from Rossio takes about 40 minutes, and the palaces are on the hill above the station. Book palace tickets in advance and be on a train back by 14:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard.

faqs.q: What can I do in Lisbon in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Alfama and the castle in the morning, then tram 15E to Belém for the Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower, back by bus 728. Or stay central: Alfama, the Sé, the Baixa, tram 28 and Chiado.

faqs.q: Is Lisbon safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes, with the usual care. Pickpockets work tram 28, tram 15E and the busy squares, and street sellers offer fake drugs in the Baixa. Watch your footing on the cobbles.
